title: Eval-driven Output Contract Guardian
creator: Ava Patel
description: Problem: We currently detect structured-output regressions through periodic evals and ad-hoc alerts, but there is no continuous, config-aware guard that ties schema/contract quality spikes to model or serving configuration changes. This leaves rollouts (model swaps, quantization profiles, runtime kernel toggles) vulnerable to silent contract regressions that only surface in downstream logs or customer tickets.
goal: Build an Eval-driven Output Contract Guardian that continuously evaluates a targeted set of structured-output evals (JSON schema adherence + semantic field checks) against live traffic slices and links regression signals to recent model/config rollouts. Provide alerting, automatic canary hold, and a short remediation playbook for on-call and release engineers.
acceptance_criteria: Guardian runs a configurable eval suite on sampled production traffic within 10 minutes of a model/config rollout and produces a regression score compared to baseline
Regression trigger rules (thresholds, minimum sample size) can be set per-route and per-model-tag
When triggered, guardian annotates the rollout event in Console and opens a templated incident with reproducible examples and failing schema instances
Guardian supports JSON Schema validation plus three semantic checks: missing-required-fields, field-type-mismatch-after-coercion, and confidence-distribution-shift for enumerated fields
End-to-end test in staging that simulates a quantization config change causing a known schema regression and results in canary hold (no global promotion)
implementation_steps: Design eval harness adapter: lightweight runner that executes schema checks + semantic field validators against sampled responses (ENG + Evals team) - design doc: https://confluence.redwood/infr/eval-contract-guardian
Integrate with rollout events: subscribe to rollout webhook stream, enrich with model/config metadata and baseline fingerprint
Baseline creation: capture baseline pass rates per-route from the last successful stable rollout (store compressed fingerprint in S3/metadata store)
Scoring engine: compute regression delta with bootstrapped confidence intervals. Implement minimum sample size and temporal smoothing to avoid noisy shortcuts
Alerting and Console integration: surface results as annotation on rollout timeline, create templated incident in PagerDuty/console with example payloads
Canary policy enforcement: hook into rollout engine to support optional automatic hold on canary promotion when high-confidence regression detected
Operational runbook and remediation templates for on-call
Add telemetry: counters for evaluated requests, pass/fail, per-field failure rates, and regression RCA links
rollout_plan: Alpha: run guardian in read-only mode for a week across 3 low-traffic routes (no alerts) to validate false-positive characteristics
Beta: enable alerting to test-channel (sre-evals) and attach Console annotations (2 weeks)
Canary enforcement: enable optional hold for internal canaries only (1 week)
GA: turn on for all canaries and provide UI controls for per-route thresholds and PM approvals
test_plan: Unit tests for schema + semantic validators with adversarial cases (untyped numbers, nested nulls, unexpected arrays)
Synthetic regression simulation: introduce deterministic JSON mutations in staging to validate detection and canary hold
Load test: ensure guardian adapter adds <5% p50 latency to sampling pipeline at 2000 rps
Integration test: end-to-end from rollout event -> evaluation -> Console annotation -> PagerDuty trigger
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive thresholds catch regressions sooner but increase false positives; we will default to conservative thresholds and provide per-route overrides
Consideration: For privacy-sensitive routes, perform evaluations within Private deployments or use synthetic replay rather than live traffic sampling
We should avoid enforcing canary hold for public GA without multi-sig escalation path
Related work: builds on schema telemetry from ENG-16358 and structured output integrity gates from ENG-17542
